newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks scale new heights by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks scale new heights by close.

text.p: Australian shares jumped convincingly on Wednesday, led by the banks after a stronger than expected half year profit by Commonwealth Bank.
The All Ordinaries index rose 25.4 points to 2,473.5.

Commonwealth Bank reported an 11 percent rise in first half net profit to A$602 million (US$455 million). Its shares jumped 59 cents to a record high of A$14.00 before backing off to close at A$13.91, up 50 cents on the day.
"Banks are definitely the flavour of the month," said a dealer at a Melbourne brokerage. "Commonwealth Bank put in a strong profit and that lit a fire under the rest of them."
The bank sector outperformed the broader market, rising 1.8 percent compared to a overall market gain of 1.04 percent.

The remaining big banks, National Australia Bank, up 21 cents at A$16.07, Westpac Banking Corporation, up 17 cents at A$7.80, and ANZ Bank, up eight cents at A$8.30, all touched record highs before easing back.
BHP turned around from early weakness to give solid support to the market in the afternoon. Brokers said futures-related buying appeared to be the impetus for interest in Australia's biggest company.
Other results included TV broadcaster Seven Network Ltd, whose shares ended five cents higher at A$4.18 despite a 31.5 percent fall in first half net profit to A$62.98 million.

Gold/nickel miner WMC reported a 46.4 percent fall in half year net profit to A$96.5 million. Its shares were steady after the result but received a lift from general market strength in the afternoon to close 12.6 cents higher at A$7.95.
Business services group Ausdoc fell 19 cents to A$2.03 after Tuesday's late announcement by would-be suitor Brambles Industries, that it would not increase its A$2.00 per share bid.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
